subject: parameter estimates in CFA; decimal places

messages.author: 86bed3e721e46622
messages.subject: parameter estimates in CFA; decimal places
parts:
Dear all, 

A reviewer asked how we handled the issue of multiple testing with regard to factor loadings' significance. Now, I am thinking about applying some sort of multiplicity control (Cribbie, 2007) but I don't know how to obtain values of p for factor loadings that are more precise (more than three decimal places) if this is at all possible in lavaan.

Also, if someone knows a good tutorial for False Discovery Rate procedures I would appreciate it.

Best regards, 
Nikola Ć.

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: parameter estimates in CFA; decimal places
parts:
You can use parameterEstimates(), as illustrated below:

``` r
# Adapted from the help page of cfa()
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-17
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6'
# Use fewer cases for larger p-values
fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939[100:150, ])
est <- parameterEstimates(fit)
# The parameter estimate table
est
#>        lhs op     rhs   est    se     z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#> 1   visual =~      x1 1.000 0.000    NA     NA    1.000    1.000
#> 2   visual =~      x2 0.492 0.246 1.998  0.046    0.009    0.975
#> 3   visual =~      x3 0.550 0.250 2.197  0.028    0.059    1.040
#> 4  textual =~      x4 1.000 0.000    NA     NA    1.000    1.000
#> 5  textual =~      x5 1.324 0.248 5.330  0.000    0.837    1.811
#> 6  textual =~      x6 1.304 0.241 5.421  0.000    0.833    1.775
#> 7       x1 ~~      x1 0.277 0.394 0.703  0.482   -0.495    1.048
#> 8       x2 ~~      x2 1.410 0.300 4.707  0.000    0.823    1.997
#> 9       x3 ~~      x3 1.128 0.256 4.405  0.000    0.626    1.630
#> 10      x4 ~~      x4 0.616 0.144 4.276  0.000    0.334    0.899
#> 11      x5 ~~      x5 0.500 0.161 3.104  0.002    0.184    0.816
#> 12      x6 ~~      x6 0.276 0.134 2.069  0.039    0.015    0.538
#> 13  visual ~~  visual 1.040 0.466 2.232  0.026    0.127    1.952
#> 14 textual ~~ textual 0.623 0.226 2.754  0.006    0.180    1.067
#> 15  visual ~~ textual 0.399 0.157 2.539  0.011    0.091    0.708
# Extract the column of p-values
est$pvalue
#>  [1]           NA 4.568134e-02 2.805130e-02           NA 9.809103e-08
#>  [6] 5.920386e-08 4.820157e-01 2.512265e-06 1.057661e-05 1.898739e-05
#> [11] 1.906200e-03 3.851034e-02 2.559082e-02 5.894186e-03 1.112823e-02
# Extract the p-values of selected parameters
est$pvalue[c(2, 3, 5, 6)]
#> [1] 4.568134e-02 2.805130e-02 9.809103e-08 5.920386e-08
```

<sup>Created on 2024-02-07 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai
